s:
Consider the following statements about the Comptroller and Auditor General:
1. The provisions on the office are in Part V, Chapter V, Articles 148-151 of the Constitution.
2. Its official name in the Constitution is the 'Comptroller and Auditor-General of India'.
3. A single CAG auditing both Union and State accounts is a federal feature of the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: one CAG auditing both Union and State accounts is a unitary feature. The CAG is an independent constitutional authority (not a statutory body under the Finance Ministry) and heads the Indian Audit and Accounts Department.

s:
Match List-I (Article) with List-II (Content):
List-I | List-II
a. Article 148 | i. Form of accounts prescribed by the President on the CAG's advice
b. Article 149 | ii. Duties and powers, as prescribed by Parliament
c. Article 150 | iii. Appointment, oath, term and removal of the CAG
d. Article 151 | iv. Audit reports to the President and the Governor
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: 148 – appointment, oath, removal, post-retirement bar (148(4)), expenses charged (148(6)); 149 – duties and powers (CAG Act, 1971); 150 – form of accounts, on the CAG's advice; 151 – reports: Union → President (151(1)), State → Governor (151(2)).

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): The CAG is not a part of the Union Executive.
Reason (R): The CAG is appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true, but R does not explain A: the Attorney General and Governors are also appointed by the President, and the AG is part of the Union Executive. The Union Executive comprises the President, VP, PM, Council of Ministers and Attorney General – not the CAG (nor the Speaker, who is part of Parliament).

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under the CAG Act, 1971 the CAG holds office for six years or till the age of 65, whichever is earlier.
2. The Chief Election Commissioner has the same term as the CAG.
3. Members of a State Public Service Commission hold office for six years or till the age of 62.
4. The 15th Amendment, 1963 raised the retirement age of High Court judges from 60 to 62.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
x: All four are correct. The CAG's term is the longest compared with the President, VP and a Lok Sabha member (5 years); UPSC members and the CEC/ECs also have 6 years or 65; a Supreme Court judge retires at 65.

s:
Consider the following statements about the CAG:
1. He is removed in like manner and on like grounds as a Supreme Court judge, under Article 148(1) read with Article 124(4).
2. He holds office during the pleasure of the President.
3. The Constitution prescribes the same qualifications for him as for a Supreme Court judge.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Only 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: he is removed only on an address by both Houses with special majority for proved misbehaviour or incapacity – not at the President's pleasure. 3 is wrong: the Constitution prescribes no qualifications for the CAG.

s:
Match List-I (CAG) with List-II (Fact):
List-I | List-II
a. V. Narahari Rao | i. 11th CAG, author of 'When Audit Matters'
b. A.K. Chanda | ii. 3rd CAG, later Chairman of the 3rd Finance Commission
c. Vinod Rai | iii. 15th CAG, since 21 November 2024
d. K. Sanjay Murthy | iv. First CAG of independent India (1948)
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: V. Narahari Rao – first CAG from 15 August 1948; A.K. Chanda – 3rd CAG, later 3rd FC Chairman; Vinod Rai – 11th CAG (2008-13, 2G report), wrote 'When Audit Matters'; K. Sanjay Murthy – 15th CAG since 21 November 2024.

s:
Consider the following statements about the audit reports of the CAG:
1. Reports on the accounts of a State are submitted to the Governor under Article 151(2).
2. Union reports go to the President, who causes them to be laid before Parliament, after which the Public Accounts Committee examines them.
3. Reports relating to public sector undertakings are examined by the Estimates Committee.
4. The three Union reports are on Appropriation Accounts, Finance Accounts and Public Undertakings.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
x: Three are correct. 3 is wrong: PSU reports are examined by the Committee on Public Undertakings. There is no CAG report on Estimates; the sequence is CAG → President → both Houses → PAC → Action Taken Notes.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Public Accounts Committee:
1. It was set up in 1921 under the Government of India Act, 1919.
2. It has 22 members – 15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha – elected by single transferable vote.
3. A Minister can be a member of the Committee.
4. Its Chairman is appointed by the Speaker and has been from the Opposition since 1967.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: no Minister can be a member of the PAC. Its 2026-27 chair is K.C. Venugopal.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): The recommendations of the Public Accounts Committee are not binding on the executive.
Reason (R): The CAG attends the meetings of the Public Accounts Committee and assists it in examining his reports.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true, but R does not explain A. PAC recommendations are advisory (hence the backlog of Action Taken Notes); the CAG's role as the PAC's 'friend, philosopher and guide' does not make them non-binding.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The CAG (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act was enacted in 1971.
2. Its 1976 amendment, in force from 1 March 1976, separated accounts from audit.
3. The Controller General of Accounts, who now compiles Union accounts, gives the Finance Minister a quarterly analytical review.
4. The CAG still keeps most State accounts.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
x: Three are correct. 3 is wrong: the Controller General of Accounts (Finance Ministry) gives the Finance Minister a monthly analytical review.

s:
Match List-I (Type of audit) with List-II (What it tests):
List-I | List-II
a. Legal and regulatory (compliance) audit | i. Whether the accounts are true
b. Financial attest audit | ii. Economy, efficiency and effectiveness
c. Propriety audit | iii. Money legally available and spent as the rules require
d. Performance audit | iv. Wisdom, faithfulness and economy; flags extravagance
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Compliance – legal availability and spending by rules; financial attest – true accounts (both obligatory); propriety – wisdom, faithfulness, economy (discretionary); performance – the 3 Es (discretionary, 2006 OM).

s:
Consider the following statements about audits by the CAG:
1. Compliance audit and financial attest audit are obligatory.
2. Propriety audit is discretionary.
3. Performance audit is obligatory.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: performance audit (economy, efficiency, effectiveness) is discretionary, under a 2006 OM.

s:
Match List-I (Body / item) with List-II (How it is audited):
List-I | List-II
a. Damodar Valley Corporation | i. CAG accepts a certificate of the competent authority
b. IFCI | ii. Private auditors on the CAG's advice, with CAG supplementary audit
c. Life Insurance Corporation | iii. Directly by the CAG
d. Secret service expenditure | iv. Wholly by private auditors, no CAG role
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: DVC (and ONGC) – audited directly by the CAG; IFCI (and Central Warehousing Corp.) – private auditors on the CAG's advice + supplementary audit; LIC (and RBI) – wholly private; secret service expenditure – the CAG accepts a certificate.

s:
Consider the following statements about the CAG of India:
1. Unlike Britain's C&AG, he has no control over the issue of money from the Consolidated Fund, so he is only an Auditor General.
2. He can disallow irregular expenditure and enforce recovery of the amount.
3. He audits the accounts of local bodies only on the request of the President or the Governor.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the CAG cannot disallow expenditure, enforce recovery, prosecute or suo motu investigate corruption – he only reports to the legislature. His audit is ex-post.

s:
Consider the following statements about the independence of the CAG:
1. His salary equals that of a Supreme Court judge, as provided in the Second Schedule.
2. The administrative expenses of his office, including staff pensions, are voted annually by the Lok Sabha.
3. After retirement he may be appointed to head a government commission.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
x: Only one (1) is correct. 2 is wrong: his salary and the office's expenses are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India (Art. 148(6)) and are non-votable. 3 is wrong: Art. 148(4) is a complete bar on further office under the GoI or any State; it is retired judges who often head commissions.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. CAG audit reports on the accounts of Andhra Pradesh are submitted to the Governor of Andhra Pradesh.
2. After 2014, reports on the accounts of undivided Andhra Pradesh went to the Governors of both AP and Telangana.
3. In the CAG's State Finances report for 2022-23, AP's revenue receipts were Rs 1,57,768 crore, own tax revenue (Rs 78,026 crore) being about half.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: All three are correct (Art. 151(2)). AP's own tax was 5.92% and central transfers 5.64% of GSDP in 2022-23.

Match List-I (CAG report) with List-II (Associated fact):
List-I | List-II
a. 2G spectrum (2010) | i. Presumptive loss of Rs 1.76 lakh crore
b. Coal blocks (2012) | ii. Redacted pricing
c. Rafale (2019) | iii. Faulty bio-toilets at 491 of 512 stations
d. Report No. 31 of 2026 (Railways) | iv. Loss of Rs 1.86 lakh crore
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: 2G (2010) – presumptive loss Rs 1.76 lakh crore; coal blocks (2012) – Rs 1.86 lakh crore; Rafale (2019) – redacted pricing; Report No. 31 of 2026 – bio-toilets faulty at 491 of 512 stations (PAC under K.C. Venugopal pulled up the Railways).
